# Illustrations

Hand-drawn characters for moments with room to breathe.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/Illustrations.mdx`

## Overview

PLUS illustrations are 12 hand-drawn spot characters: five for the SMART areas and seven math symbols. Each character's body takes its area or accent token, so it adapts to Light and Dark. See Illustration for props, sizes and code. A low-fidelity illustration of the UI uses basic shapes in mostly gray, never a real screenshot; see the Illustration kit. Decide first that an illustration is needed.

## Characters

The five SMART characters each stand for an area; the seven math characters stand for general moments and take an accent hue.

| Moment | Character |
| --- | --- |
| A lesson, card or page about one SMART area | That area's character: `mastering-content`, `advocacy`, `technology`, `relationships` or `social-emotional`. |
| General moments: empty state, welcome, completion | A math character: `dot`, `approximately-equal`, `root`, `all`, `pi`, `equal` or `divider`. |

## Color and SMART mapping

All 12 bodies sit at one mid strength so the set reads equally light in Light and Dark. SMART characters take `color/background/competency/<area>/subtle`. Math characters take `color/background/accent/<hue>/subtle` (red, blue, green or purple) and never a SMART hue. Line work takes `color/icon/subtle`.

| Character | Body token |
| --- | --- |
| mastering content | `--ds-background-competency-mastering-content-subtle` |
| advocacy | `--ds-background-competency-advocacy-subtle` |
| technology | `--ds-background-competency-technology-tools-subtle` |
| relationships | `--ds-background-competency-relationship-subtle` |
| social emotional | `--ds-background-competency-social-emotional-subtle` |
| dot · pi | `--ds-background-accent-red-subtle` |
| approximately equal · equal | `--ds-background-accent-blue-subtle` |
| root · divider | `--ds-background-accent-green-subtle` |
| all | `--ds-background-accent-purple-subtle` |
| Face, arms and legs (all) | `--ds-icon-subtle` |

## Usage

| Where | Illustration | Guidance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Empty state | Yes | One character above the message: 96 on a card, 160 on a page. |
| Onboarding and tours | Yes | One character per step: 160 or 240. |
| Completion and encouragement | Yes | A finished session or met goal: 160 or 240. |
| SMART area header | Yes | The area’s own character, at 48 or 96. |
| Tables, forms and toolbars | No | Working surfaces. Use icons or copy instead. |
| Inline errors and buttons | No | These need words, not mood. Use a Banner. |

- Use the `Illustration` component; never detach or recolor its parts.
- Pick a size from the scale and scale uniformly.
- Reuse existing characters first. Adding a new character requires design lead approval.
- An illustration works with the copy and never replaces it.
- Other visuals have their own components: `Avatar` for people, `Icon` for actions, `Logo` for brand, `Image` for photos.

## Do and don't

### Match the character to its SMART area

The body color stands for the area, so a character only appears with its own area.

Do: The technology character with the Technology & tools lesson.
Don't: The mastering content character on a Relationships lesson.

### Keep the proportions

Scale with the size; the limbs and texture distort when stretched.

Do: Scaled uniformly to a size on the scale.
Don't: Stretched to fill a banner.

### One character per moment

A single character carries the mood; a crowd competes with the message.

Do: One character above the empty-state message.
Don't: Four characters crowding one empty state; a collage like this belongs on a marketing page, not in the product.

## Accessibility

- Keep an illustration decorative, hidden from assistive technology, wherever the copy beside it says the same thing.
- Name an illustration that carries meaning on its own, using the component's `title`, and say what it shows in a few words.
- Never put the only copy of information in an illustration. The words carry it.
